hero.lead: A desert nation of 3.09 million that signed a $10 billion green hydrogen agreement in 2023, and where four in ten citizens still have no electricity.

capital.heading: 10 instruments. A hydrogen project, the grid it will need, a railway and a fund for community conservation.

record.text: Debt-to-GDP ratio, FY2025/26, down from 67.3%; total public debt is projected at N$201.7 billion, 68.7% of GDP, for FY2026/27 (Mid-Year Budget Review, 22 October 2026)
Hyphen green hydrogen project: Feasibility and Implementation Agreement signed 26 May 2023, for 2 million tonnes of green ammonia a year at full scale
Transmission Expansion and Energy Storage Project, approved 6 May 2024: a $100 million IBRD loan with grants and a Green Climate Fund loan
Namibia for Life, launched May 2026: Africa’s first Project Finance for Permanence, for community conservation on more than 20% of the land

register.name: Eurobond, redeemed
register.text: Namibia redeemed its $750 million Eurobond in October 2025, as the IMF recorded in March 2026. The Ministry of Finance counts the redemption among the foreign debt repayments of 2025/26.

register.name: Transmission Expansion and Energy Storage Project
register.detail: Approved 6 May 2024 · IBRD loan of $100 million · $138.5 million project with an IBRD Global Public Goods grant and a Green Climate Fund loan and grant
register.note: A second Auas–Kokerboom line and utility-scale battery storage
register.text: Namibia’s first World Bank financed energy project, carried out by NamPower: a second Auas–Kokerboom transmission line, a utility-scale battery storage facility and support to prepare bankable renewable projects. It lets more clean power reach the grid in a nation where 59.3% of citizens have electricity (2024).

register.name: Namibia Renewable Energy Scale Up Support Project
register.detail: Grant from the Energy Sector Management Assistance Program · Recipient NamPower · Advance of $300,000 disbursed 14 November 2023
register.note: Studies and procurement advice for renewable power
register.text: A World Bank administered grant for preparatory studies and for advice on procuring variable renewable energy projects. It prepares the clean generation that energy for every citizen will need.

register.name: Transport Infrastructure Improvement Project, phase two (railway)
register.detail: Approved 31 October 2023 · Loan · 51.8% of the project cost; the Government of Namibia provides 48.2%
register.text: An African Development Bank loan for the second phase of the national railway upgrade, including 207 km of new track. Cheaper freight lowers the cost of goods and supports trade and jobs, and so livelihoods.

register.name: Hyphen Hydrogen Energy, front-end engineering design loan
register.detail: Approval announced 9 December 2025 · Loan from the Sustainable Energy Fund for Africa
register.note: Phase one: 3.75 GW of renewables and 1.5 GW of electrolysers
register.text: An African Development Bank loan to Hyphen Hydrogen Energy for front-end engineering design of solar and wind generation, battery storage, electrolysers and desalination. It moves a green ammonia project valued at more than $10 billion towards construction.

register.name: Hyphen Hydrogen Energy green hydrogen project
register.detail: Signed 26 May 2023 · Feasibility and Implementation Agreement · Approved by Cabinet 23 May 2023 · Government stake of 24% completed 18 December 2024
register.note: 2 million tonnes of green ammonia a year at full scale
register.text: A privately developed green hydrogen and ammonia project, in which the Government of Namibia completed the purchase of a 24% stake in December 2024. The African Development Bank valued it at more than $10 billion in December 2025, when it lent $10 million for front-end engineering design. Its first phase includes 3.75 GW of renewable generation and 1.5 GW of electrolysers.

register.name: Namibia for Life
register.detail: Launched May 2026 · Africa’s first Project Finance for Permanence · Up to 100 communal conservancies · May grow to more than $75 million
register.note: More than 283,000 conservancy members, more than 20% of the land
register.text: A long-term financing initiative for community-led conservation across up to 100 communal conservancies covering more than 20% of Namibia, backed by the Government, philanthropies, the Green Climate Fund, the Global Environment Facility and Germany. The Community Conservation Fund of Namibia counts it as N$1 billion of long-term conservation financing. It reaches more than 283,000 conservancy members, for whom conservation is a livelihood.
by: Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism

register.name: SDG Namibia One Fund, Zhero Molecules Walvis Bay development funding
register.detail: Signed 19 December 2025 · Development funding agreement · Final investment decision targeted for 2027 · Operation expected 2030
register.note: 500,000 tonnes of green ammonia a year, near Walvis Bay
register.text: Namibia’s green hydrogen fund commits up to $5.15 million to develop a green ammonia project near Walvis Bay in the Erongo Region. The fund is managed by Climate Fund Managers with Invest International and the Environmental Investment Fund of Namibia, and holds €65 million of early-stage development funding.

register.name: European Union investment in the SDG Namibia One Fund
register.detail: Announced 4 September 2024 · After Invest International and USAID · Fund target $1 billion of blended finance
register.text: The European Union invests €25 million in SDG Namibia One, the blended finance fund for green hydrogen whose manager is co-owned by the Environmental Investment Fund of Namibia. The fund aims to raise $1 billion for the sector.

register.name: SDG Namibia One Fund, 24% stake in the Hyphen project
register.detail: Agreed 22 December 2023 · Acquisition completed 18 December 2024 · Initial development funding
register.text: SDG Namibia One took a 24% stake in the Hyphen green hydrogen project, backed by initial development funding of €23 million, giving the Government of Namibia direct ownership. The project is planned to produce 2 million tonnes of green ammonia a year from about 7 GW of mostly wind and solar power.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Half live in towns and cities.

items.name: NamWater
items.text: The state-owned company in charge of bulk water supply to Namibia, with 195 water supply schemes, 37 treatment plants and 6,996 km of pipelines. It recorded revenue of N$2.2 billion in the year to 31 March 2025.

items.name: Shack Dwellers Federation of Namibia
items.text: A federation through which low-income Namibians build their own homes, supported by FNB Namibia, the Pupkewitz Foundation and Ohorongo Cement with N$1 million a year each. It has delivered more than 530 houses valued at over N$23 million over the past decade (2026).

items.name: Solarcentury Africa, Gerus solar plant
items.text: A 19.3 MWp solar plant in commercial operation, wholly owned by Solarcentury Africa, whose power is sold into the Southern African Power Pool by Solarcentury Trading. It is expected to produce about 50.8 GWh of clean electricity a year, enough for more than 14,000 Namibian homes.

items.name: Mediclinic Windhoek
items.text: A private hospital in Windhoek, part of Mediclinic Southern Africa, offering a comprehensive range of medical and surgical services. It has served the Namibian community for more than 35 years.

items.name: Letshego Namibia
items.text: A lender that opened in 2002 as Edu Loan Namibia and is 79% owned by Letshego Holdings. IFC provided a $50 million facility in 2021 so that it could extend affordable housing finance to more than 4,000 Namibians.
